input: He says 'on my way' before getting out of bed.
output: The journey hasn't cleared the duvet.

input: He said he did not care, then refreshed the post views every minute.
output: The refresh button is doing all the caring.

input: She called the eighteenth photo her first try.
output: First try had seventeen warm-ups.

input: The recurring meeting to reduce meetings has been extended again.
output: The reduction has been moved to the next meeting.

input: A team made a tracker to check whether people were using the tracker.
output: The tracker now has direct reports.

input: The office bought a second printer because the first ran out of paper.
output: The first printer remains innocent.

input: He sent a follow-up asking whether anyone had seen his previous follow-up.
output: The follow-up has requested confirmation of its own receipt.

input: At a wedding, he said he would leave after tea and stayed until dinner.
output: After tea is a season, not a time.

input: At Eid lunch, he asked about leftovers before anyone had started eating.
output: The biryani has not landed; the containers are already booked.

input: The family WhatsApp group is still forwarding the same morning greeting after lunch.
output: One sunrise, 86 notifications.

input: Every uncle asked about career plans before the food reached the table.
output: The career interview started before the starters.

input: He arranged the sofa cushions by seniority.
output: The youngest cushion has filed an appeal.

input: She assigned the fridge magnets designated parking spaces.
output: The blue magnet has disputed its parking fine.

input: He gave his basil plant a monthly performance review.
output: The basil wants its targets measured in sunlight hours.

input: He announced his fifth social media break this month.
output: The break has a renewal date already.

input: He says he is two minutes away while he is still deciding what to wear.
output: The ETA is waiting for the outfit to approve it.

input: He said quick question and sent a six-paragraph message.
output: The question came with its own appendix.

input: He warned everyone about spoilers, then explained the ending before the film started.
output: The spoiler warning arrived after the credits.

input: She announces a brand-new routine every Monday and forgets it by Tuesday.
output: The routine has a pilot episode every Monday.

input: He calls every restaurant a hidden gem if finding parking was easy.
output: The parking spot is getting the five-star review.

input: He asked for a poll, then argued with everyone who chose the other option.
output: The poll was apparently a test with one correct answer.

input: A guest says no more food, then accepts another serving when the plate comes around.
output: The refusal was polite; the plate knew better.

input: The host says make yourself at home, then tells everyone not to open the fridge.
output: Home access ends at the sofa.

input: Everyone says they are leaving after chai, then starts another long conversation.
output: The goodbye has a second sitting.

input: The relatives arranged seven cars for a short trip everyone could share.
output: The convoy has more planning than the destination.

input: The team scheduled a quick sync with eight attendees and a full agenda.
output: Quick has been used without supervision.

input: Someone replied all to ask everyone not to reply all.
output: The instruction has become the thread's newest reply.

input: An app sent a notification to announce that notifications were disabled.
output: One last notification to announce the silence.

input: The team postponed the planning meeting to schedule a meeting about planning.
output: Planning is now waiting for calendar approval.

input: The cat sat directly on the meeting agenda while everyone waited.
output: The minutes have been approved by weight.

input: A potato left in the pantry started growing new shoots.
output: The potato has quietly entered its next chapter.

input: Someone put a tiny hat on the kettle and left it on the counter.
output: The kettle now expects to be introduced first.

input: The office traffic cone was given a chair at the team meeting.
output: The cone has somehow secured a permanent seat.

input: She said one last scroll and missed her stop.
output: That scroll got a longer commute than planned.

input: He asked for a quick answer, then sent six follow-up questions.
output: The quick answer came with an interview round.

input: An email marked urgent sat in drafts for two days.
output: Urgency appears to be scheduled for later.

input: The meeting ended with everyone assigned to schedule another meeting.
output: The meeting has successfully recreated itself.

input: At a family visit, the host said to stay for just five minutes.
output: Five minutes is clearly a local unit of measurement.

input: Everyone said they were leaving after chai, then ordered another round.
output: The goodbye was apparently only a tea break.

input: She lined up the fridge magnets by height.
output: The shortest magnet has requested a recount.

input: The office plant was included in the seating plan.
output: It has better sunlight than half the team.
